title: Late Fees on Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing Accounts: Grace Period, Courtesy Waiver and Reversal
content:
This guidance note sets out when a late fee arises on a Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing account, when it may be waived or must be reversed, and how a reversal is made.

## When a late fee arises

A scheduled payment not posted in full by the end of the plan's grace period draws one late fee for that statement period. A late fee may be assessed only when the scheduled payment is still unpaid after the grace period that follows its due date. Calendar days are counted from the day after the due date, and a payment posted on the last grace day is on time. No late fee applies to a period covered by an approved hardship deferral.

| Element of the grace test | Basis |
|---|---|
| Event the clock starts from | The due date of that statement period's scheduled payment, from the account's payment due day |
| Length | The plan's late-fee grace period, in calendar days |
| Counting | Day 1 is the day after the due date |
| Payment posted on the last grace day | On time; no late fee |
| Scheduled payment still unpaid after the last grace day | One late fee for that statement period may be assessed |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical).** With a due date on the 5th of a month and a 10-day grace period, the last grace day is the 15th. A payment posted in full on the 15th is on time. A scheduled payment still unpaid on the 16th draws one late fee for that statement period.

## The amount clause, retired for plans without a promotion

> The late fee is the plan's fixed fee or the stated share of the scheduled payment, whichever is lower, rounded to the cent.

For a late fee on an account whose plan carries no promotion (a fixed-rate or low-payment plan), this clause is no longer in force; the amount of such a late fee is governed by the current late fee assessment basis of Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing. A late fee on an account whose plan carries a promotion remains under this clause. The grace period, the one-fee-per-period limit, the hardship exclusion, the courtesy waiver and the error reversal in this note remain in force on every plan.

## Courtesy waiver

A correctly assessed late fee may be waived once as a courtesy when the account paid on time for at least the stated number of periods immediately before and the plan's courtesy limit in the preceding 365 days has not been used.

- *Paid on time for the periods immediately before*: the number of consecutive statement periods immediately before the one handled in which the scheduled payment posted in full by its due date, with no late fee assessed, counting back from the most recent.
- *Courtesy limit used*: the late fees on the account reversed as a courtesy (fees that had been correctly assessed) in the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date, compared with the plan's courtesy waiver allowance.

## Error reversal

A late fee assessed in error, such as one on a period whose payment posted on time, is reversed whatever the courtesy count.

## One reversal per fee

A fee is reversed at most once, in full, by a reversal naming it. Whether a fee has already been reversed is read from the reversals on the account that name that fee.

## Hypothetical courtesy case

On a plan allowing 1 courtesy waiver in any rolling 365 days and requiring 6 on-time periods, an account whose 6 periods before the late one were all paid in full by their due dates, and which has had no courtesy reversal in the preceding 365 days, meets both conditions, and its correctly assessed late fee may be waived once. The figures are illustrative.
